page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per vCPU. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes 260 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the multi-core performance of this instance in the top tier, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core tests and a PassMark CPU score of 115,368.08. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only large block speeds reaching 577.03 GB/sec and write speeds at 247.9 GB/sec. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which accelerate workloads like LLM inference and cryptography. For instance, LLM inference for prompt processing on a large 70B model achieves 38.91 tokens/sec, placing it in the top tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores falling into the average category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-192 offers high resource density for highly parallelized workloads, making it a viable alternative to GPU-accelerated instances for certain CPU-based AI inference tasks. The primary tradeoff is the complete lack of local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, large-scale Redis deployments, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-density general-purpose server featuring 192 vCPUs and 720 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 96 physical cores, it delivers top-tier multi-core performance and exceptional memory bandwidth, reaching 577.03 GB/sec for large block reads. The integration of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 enables strong performance in cryptography and CPU-based LLM inference, such as processing 38.91 tokens/sec on a 70B model. However, the instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, and its single-core performance remains average. This configuration is highly efficient for parallelized workloads, including software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput web serving, offering a robust CPU-only alternative for compute-heavy enterprise applications.
